paragraphs: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak. (A tanna cited in a baraita.)

In [Kiddushin 54a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.54a.6), the baraita reads: “R. Y. son of R. Y. said: The stones of Jerusalem that fell are subject to me’ilah—the words of Rabbi Meir,” etc. Hyman is certain that this is a copyist’s error and that it should read: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak recited the teaching.” On that reading, Hyman identifies him as an amora and a student of Rabbi Yochanan. Hyman quotes [Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yoma.3.7.4) as follows: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rav Yitzchak; Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s proposed “recited the teaching” makes Yishmael a transmitter of the baraita. Me’ilah means misuse of consecrated property.

The linked Kiddushin gives Rabbi Yishmael bar Rabbi Yitzchak. The linked Yerushalmi gives Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2268&lang=en) gives Yishmael bar Rav Yitzchak in its heading and directs readers to Shimon.
